problem: Existing embodied or interactive platforms each lack something needed for multimodal learning in a realistic context. Game and maze sandboxes (ALE, Malmo, DeepMind Lab, ViZDoom) have no realistic household context. Photorealistic household simulators (AI2-THOR with 32 houses, Matterport3D Simulator with 90) are small-scale. The concurrent House3D, also built on SUNCG, lacks sound, true physics and object interaction. No major interactive platform renders high-fidelity audio.
motivation: Human learning is interactive, multimodal and driven by concept-to-concept context, for example that forks are in kitchens, which are near living rooms. Scale of data has repeatedly proven key for generalization and sim-to-real transfer. The authors argue that 'virtual embodiment' needs a single large-scale platform that combines vision, audio, semantics, physics and multi-agent interaction inside realistic houses.
key_idea: HoME turns the ~45,622 hand-designed SUNCG house layouts into an open-source, OpenAI Gym-compatible interactive environment. It provides modular rendering (Panda3D), ray-traced acoustics (EVERT), semantic annotation and physics (Bullet) engines, with multi-agent support.
insight: This is a platform/position paper with no experiments or ablations. The main takeaway is a design argument. First, it trades photorealism for scale: SUNCG's simpler graphics give tens of thousands of layouts and faster-than-real-time rendering on a single CPU core. Second, it makes the modality engines independent, pluggable modules over one dataset loader. Its comparison table positions HoME as the only listed environment combining 3D, context, large scale, speed, customizability, physics and acoustics, though it is not photorealistic.
method: Dataset loader over SUNCG: 45,622 house layouts and 750,000+ rooms of 24 kinds, with objects from 84 categories (avg >14 per room), sometimes multi-floor.
Rendering engine (Panda3D, Python bindings): RGB (several shader presets) and depth images, with textured materials, multi-source lighting and shadows.

Acoustic engine (EVERT real-time acoustic ray-tracing): supports multiple microphones and sources, distance attenuation, frequency-dependent material absorption/reflection and atmospheric air absorption. Outputs stereo sound frames per agent; sources can be artificial (e.g. TV static) or environment-driven (e.g. surface-dependent footsteps).

Semantic engine: per-object text descriptions plus color (16 basic / ~130 intermediate / ~950 detailed xkcd colors), generic and detailed category, material (20 classes, largest surface area), size (small/medium/large via volume histogram per category) and GT location. Also dense segmentation over SUNCG's 187 fine-grained categories.

Physics engine (Bullet 3): each object gets either a bounding-box or an exact-mesh rigid body, with gravity from volume-based weight estimates and collisions. Agents can pick up, drop and push objects; the engine outputs positions and velocities.

Gym-compatible Python framework: spawns one or more agents in randomly selected houses, with actions for moving, looking and object interaction. Runs faster than real time on one CPU core, with GPU acceleration and parallel environment instances.

setting.training_data: n/a (platform built on the SUNCG dataset, 45,622 house layouts)
setting.observation: platform provides RGB (shader presets), depth, stereo/multichannel audio, semantic segmentation, object attributes/text descriptions, agent/object physical state
setting.action_space: moving, looking, object interaction (pick up, drop, push); exact discretization not specified
setting.privileged: n/a (platform exposes GT semantics, object locations and positions if tasks choose to use them)

numbers_note: No experimental results are reported; this is a platform/workshop paper. The only table is a qualitative feature comparison of environments. Speed is claimed only qualitatively ('faster than real-time on a single-core CPU'), with no benchmarks.
results: No quantitative results. The paper's claims are qualitative: HoME covers 45,622 SUNCG houses, about 500× the 90 of Matterport3D Simulator and about 1400× the 32 of AI2-THOR. It is claimed to be the first major interactive platform with high-fidelity ray-traced audio. It adds physics and object interaction that the concurrent House3D lacks, and runs faster than real time on a single CPU core.
limitations: Not photorealistic: SUNCG synthetic graphics widen the sim-to-real gap compared with scan-based environments such as Matterport3D. SUNCG was later withdrawn from public distribution, which limits reproducibility.

No tasks, benchmarks, baselines or speed measurements are provided. The listed applications (instruction following, EQA-style VQA, dialogue, Pied Piper sound following, multi-agent communication) are only proposed.
The action space, reward design and physics fidelity (volume-based weight approximations, bounding-box bodies) are only loosely specified.
